title: Two Sum
spaceBreakdown: unordered_map seen: up to n entries → O(n)
approach: Walk the array once; for each number look up target - number in a hash map of values seen so far, then store the current number with its index.
hints: For each number, which other value would complete the pair?
Checking every earlier number is O(n²). Can you look that value up in O(1)?
Keep a map from value → index of the numbers you've already passed.
Look up target - nums[i] BEFORE inserting nums[i], so a number is never paired with itself (e.g. [3,3], target 6).

followUps.q: What if the array were sorted?
followUps.a: Use two pointers from both ends: O(n) time and O(1) extra space.

followUps.q: What if you must return all pairs, not just one?
followUps.a: Keep counts in the map and emit a pair for each earlier occurrence of the complement.

followUps.q: What if the input is too big for memory?
followUps.a: Sort externally and use two pointers, or partition by hash into chunks that fit.
